rv.q: These are substantial performances in a purposeful production, don't get me wrong, but they have little room for play.

This production exalts so much of what “Hair” is about. But I’m not sure it’s aware it is so guarded, earnest, moody and cynical, that when the cast sings the finale, “Let the Sunshine In,” they don’t.
In short, this cast is having a blast and so will you.
The show is infectious, and you leave it feeling loopy and swingy, with your hair a little longer.
By now, Kokandy has established itself as one of the best companies in the city for musicals. They elevate everything they take on, and their instincts are on point for almost all the changes.
If the success of a production of Hair lies in how much we feel for Claude, though, this one doesn't fully succeed, at least not in the riser section of the audience where I was seated.
Kokandy's Hair elevates the best moments of the material without allowing the more dated ones to overstay their welcome.
Kokandy Productions delivers an energetic and visually engaging revival of Hair that embraces the musical's enduring message of peace, love, and individuality.
In the end, while this may not be your grandfather's 'Hair,' Kokandy still delivers a powerful, resonant message.
I felt the overall performance was entertaining and exhilarating.
On the upside, this cast is always in the moment, earnestly conveying the feeling of community and totally present in everything they sing, say or do.
I know that many people will be anxious to see how they handle the end of the first act, but I want you to know that what they do is special, very special and thought-provoking.
The Kokandy cast, as always, delivers on vocal quality and has put their own spin on this now classic musical.
For those that are looking for a well-conceived production of Hair or it's your first time seeing the show, this probably isn't the production for you.
